question_text: The transmissivity $T$ of a transparent material 15 mm thick to normally incident light is 0.80 . If the index of refraction of this material is 1.5, compute the thickness of material that will yield a transmissivity of 0.70. All reflection losses should be considered.The unit of the answer is mm.
response:
## Result

The calculation gives:

$$l_2 = 15 \cdot \frac{\ln(0.70/0.9216)}{\ln(0.80/0.9216)} = 15 \cdot \frac{\ln(0.75955)}{\ln(0.86806)} \approx 29.16 \text{ mm}$$

The absorption coefficient is positive ($\alpha \approx 0.00904\;\text{mm}^{-1}$), so increasing thickness reduces transmissivity — consistent with needing a thicker slab to drop $T$ from 0.80 to 0.70.

$$\boxed{29.16}$$
